ev: اعلم أن ورشا كان يميل فتحة الراء قليلا
بإخلاص الفتح للراء في جميع ما تقدم والله أعلم
items.note: Warsh gives a slight imāla to the fatḥa of a rāʾ after a fixed kasra, or after a silent letter that follows a kasra or a silent yāʾ, with or without tanwīn (الآخرة, السحر, الخيرات). He gives a pure fatḥa in the words with a letter of raising, a foreign word or a doubled rāʾ (الصراط, إبراهيم, قطرا); the book lists them, and adds بشرر in al-Mursalāt with the imāla and أولي الضرر in al-Nisāʾ without.
items.chapter: باب ذكر مذهب ورش في الراءات

items.note: On stopping, a rāʾ with a fatḥa, ḍamma or sukūn keeps its connected value; a rāʾ with a kasra is light with rawm and full with sukūn, except after a kasra, a silent yāʾ, or an inclined fatḥa (بشرر) on Warsh's way, where it is light in both. The book states the rest as the rule of readers other than Warsh, not by name.
items.chapter: باب ذكر مذهب ورش في الراءات

ev: اعلم أن ورشا كان يغلظ اللام

forms.desc: بفتح هذه اللام من غير إشباع

items.note: Warsh gives a full lām to a lām with a fatḥa after a ṣād, ṭāʾ or ẓāʾ that is itself silent or has a fatḥa (الصلاة, الطلاق, ظلم). The book allows both full and light in a verse-ending word in suras that end in a yāʾ (فصلى), the light being the more analogical.

ev: باب ذكر مذهب ورش في الراءات مجملا
وكل راء وليتها فتحة أو ضمة
لها إذا تطرفت وكانت لازمة في الوقف حكم أذكره بعد إن شاء الله تعالى
skipped.why: agreement of all readers: the rāʾ after a fatḥa or ḍamma is full, after a fixed kasra and without a letter of raising it is light, and a rāʾ with a kasra is light in connected reading
agreement of all readers: the lām of the name Allāh is full after a fatḥa or ḍamma and light after a kasra, and every other lām is light
